data.name: Aaishaht
data.gender_notes: Aaishaht is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Aaisha is the name of a prominent Sahabiyyat (female companion) of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). She was known for her knowledge, wisdom, and courage. The name Aaisha means 'living soul'. The name Aaishaht carries the meaning “Living Soul” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Aaishaht usually hope their child will grow to embody living soul and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name signifying a lively soul connected to Allah.
data.etymology: Aaishaht belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Living Soul.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aaishaht total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_arabic.name: عائشةت
in_arabic.meaning: عائشةت تعني الحياة السعيدة والمرضية لله تعالى
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم عائشةت مشتق من الجذر العربي ع-ي-ش، ويعني الحياة السعيدة والمرضية لله تعالى. ورد ذكر هذا الجذر في القرآن الكريم في سورة البقرة الآية 124، وفي الحديث النبوي الشريف عن عائشة بنت أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنها. يعتبر اسم عائشةت من الأسماء المحببة في الثقافة الإسلامية، حيث يرتبط بالسعادة والرضا الإلهي.

in_urdu.name: عائشہٹ
in_urdu.meaning: عائشہٹ کا مطلب ہے خوشحال زندگی گزارنا

in_english.name: Aaishaht
in_english.meaning: Happy and pleasing life to Allah
in_english.long_meaning: The name Aaishaht is derived from the Arabic root 'a-y-sh', meaning happy and pleasing life to Allah. This root is mentioned in the Quran and is associated with Aisha bint Abu Bakr, one of the wives of Prophet Muhammad. The name holds significant spiritual and cultural importance in Islamic tradition, symbolizing happiness and divine pleasure. It is widely used across Muslim cultures, reflecting a rich history and tradition.
